test_title: PYST 20: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Industrial Sector in India is/are correct?

1. According to National Manufacturing Policy 2011, every job created in the manufacturing sector creates two-three additional jobs in related activities.

2. Industries add value to the existing goods and also to the skill of labour employed in it; therefore, this sector is also considered a transformational sector.

3. As industries employ a large part of the population, industrial development is one of the preconditions for the eradication of unemployment and poverty from our country.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Manufacturing Policy 2011:** It highlights that every job created in the manufacturing sector leads to the creation of 2-3 additional jobs in related activities, emphasizing the multiplier effect of manufacturing employment.
 
• **Transformational Sector:** Industries add value to raw materials and enhance the skill set of workers, which is why the industrial sector is considered a transformational sector in economic development.
 
• **Employment & Poverty Eradication:** Industrial development plays a critical role in generating employment and is a precondition for eradicating poverty and unemployment in India.
 
• The industrial sector contributes significantly to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and serves as a backbone for the economic progress of the country.
 
• Policies like Make in India and National Manufacturing Policy aim to boost industrial growth and employment generation in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Sector Overview:**

 
 
• The industrial sector includes manufacturing, construction, mining, and utilities.
 
• It is a key driver of economic growth, accounting for approximately 25-30% of India’s GDP.
 
 
 
• **National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) 2011:**
 
 
• Aimed at increasing the share of manufacturing in GDP to 25% by 2022.
 
• Focuses on skill development, technology upgrades, and creation of National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs).
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched in September 2014 to promote manufacturing and attract foreign investments.
 
• Targets 25 priority sectors including automobiles, pharmaceuticals, and textiles.
 
 
 
• **Employment in Industrial Sector:**
 
 
• Accounts for a large segment of formal and informal employment in India.
 
• Industrial policies aim to reduce unemployment through job creation in manufacturing and allied sectors.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Industrial Development:**
 
 
• Infrastructure bottlenecks, skill gaps, and regulatory hurdles.
 
• Low levels of research and development (R&D) and technological innovation.
